Galactic Center and a Hills-mechanism origin: S5-HVS1
(Koposov et al. 2020).

S5-HVS1, ejected ≈ 5 Myr ago at ≈ 1800 km\mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }, is
the fastest-known hypervelocity star and the one most-

notes: S5-HVS1 is the only individual star the paper treats as a Galactic unbound object; it was already identified as a hypervelocity star in prior work (Koposov et al. 2020), and this paper analyzes its possible ADDD origin, so it is classified as follow_up. Other S-stars, HVSs, and simulated analogues are unnamed populations; S301 (T:p11-b3) is an S-star with no unbound claim.

S5-HVS1: The paper only gives the on-sky position of S5-HVS1 for reference in Figure 9. It also describes S5-HVS1 as ejected about 5 Myr ago at about 1800 km/s (Section 7.3), but that is an ejection speed, not a reported line-of-sight radial velocity, so it is not extracted as radial_velocity.
